_comment: Noise allowance per row for assert-perf-gate.py, on top of the 1.00
ceiling. The gate compares medians-of-medians over `runs` shots of three
arms measured in ONE job on ONE runner, so what is left to absorb is
same-machine shot-to-shot noise, not the CPU-model lottery perf-budgets.json
has to live with. A row is a breach when candidate/reference exceeds
1 + margin; the geomean over all rows gets `geomean` and nothing else.
Seeded from same-runner repeats (chromium perf-probe.yml runs=5, EPYC and
Xeon draws): the median-of-medians CV was 0.00-0.01 on int_math, js_alloc,
libm_fmod, locator_click, layout, screenshot and 0.02-0.05 on the
page-driving rows (goto_cold the widest). `tight` covers the first group,
`default` the second, `loose` the rows perf-budgets.json documents as
dispersion-bound even after repeats (webkit eval_rtt / click_force).
Every gate run prints the observed CV per row in its summary; tune a
margin from those, not from a failed run's ratio.
firefox WAS in `loose` (launch, js_alloc) and came back out once the gate
had printed enough CV columns to size the two rows. The entry was copied
from perf-budgets.json's dispersion-bound list, which is about the
cross-run CPU-model lottery — something this gate structurally does not
have, since all three arms share one job on one runner. Measured here
instead: firefox launch reads cv 0.018 / 0.028 / 0.042 across three gate
runs, so a 1.10 ceiling was 2.4-5.6x its own noise and a real 7% launch
regression would have promoted. js_alloc never took the loose margin at
all — `tight` is tested first and lists it — and at cv 0.009-0.012 it
should not: 1.03 is already about 2.5x its noise, and the 1.065 that
row read on 799bdf7 was a real regression, not spread.
webkit's two rows stay until perf-gate-webkit prints CV columns of its
own. It runs only when webkit is actually rebuilt, so every run looked at
so far reads `skipped`.
